string.text: {=iPw8cWlo}I can share my story with you, if you have the time.

{=47t2GEk5}I served a small fudai domain for twelve years. My lord was a decent man, but his chief councillors were parasites who spent more time arguing over stipends than preparing for the storm that is coming.

{=irhL16IF}When Commodore Perry arrived, I said we should modernize our troops. When Choshu began arming with Western weapons, I said we should do the same. They called me reckless. Then they bought rifles themselves and pretended it had been their idea all along.
{=YLn5hxVB}I spoke too openly in council. Now I travel without a stipend, without a master, and without patience for men who mistake caution for wisdom.
{=T07xEuQR}A noble decision!
{=cPpWwCU9}How virtue has crumbled since the old days.
{=EQzHDnlS}At any rate, I'll fight for any man willing to take the same risks that his men face.
{=y4EHUEhJ}I have not betrayed my lord. I merely refused to flatter fools.
{=fbkhftUI}You know, you'd think this place could serve proper sake, instead of this piss... Sorry, where were we? Ah yes, my story.
{=q4PcHv5B}I was born the son of a village headman, but I studied in a domain school where the teachers spoke of loyalty to the Throne and the corruption of Edo.

{=8LJhHcdn}The Shogunate signs treaties with foreigners, bows to foreign demands, and allows foreign ships into our waters. Every year the old order grows weaker, yet the officials tell us to remain calm.
{=ZshQMkvF}I have not joined any conspiracy. Not yet. But if a man truly intends to restore honor to the realm, I would hear him out before I hear another speech from a Tokugawa bureaucrat.
{=bMHFQgVE}Aye, real honor is as scarce as hen's teeth these days.
{=4u0yW6NO}A disappointing thing, that so few are willing to die for His Imperial Majesty.
{=mwP0qLdr}Let me tell you something - I'm sick of cowardice, sick of those who don't come forth to serve their Emperor.
{=9LgUgtje}The Emperor sits in Kyoto while weak men rule in his name.
{=56VPnxQd}You're a nosy one, I see.
{=NJBOYpT8}I served with a patrol force outside Osaka. We escorted tax shipments, guarded roads, and kept hot-headed young samurai from turning every argument into a blood feud.
{=QYtKUuSG}These days everyone talks about restoring this or expelling that. Fine words. But when merchants are robbed and villages burn, it is still Tokugawa officials who restore order.
{=5wQ8SVFg}The Shogunate is imperfect. So is every government ever created by men. I have no love for corrupt magistrates, but I fear chaos more than I fear reformers.
{=0SnKUaex}No doubt a sad state of affairs. So what do you do?
{=tZoZqI4J}What? Does no one respect their lords anymore?
{=DVoKPeYg}The Shogunate will stand with or without me. It has reigned for 250 years, and it will undoubtedly rule for another 1000.
{=KsvWPyis}Everyone complains about Edo until bandits appear on the road.
{=B3UQTCRE}Refill my glass and I'll tell you.
{=B3FYzxuX}A younger son of a samurai family, I was sent to Edo to study at a famous d┼ìj┼ì. Every evening the students argued politics more fiercely than they crossed swords.
{=76PZeDr8}Some swore the Emperor must rule directly. Others said the Tokugawa alone kept the peace. I came to master the blade, not speeches.
{=j8Uu9hDq}After too many duels over matters that had nothing to do with technique, I left. Steel cuts the same no matter whose crest is painted on the scabbard.
{=WcIRq8oJ}Indeed. Nobody is more important than a skilled swordsman.
{=CrgC7TT9}Resentment is poison to a friendship. Men must learn to follow the natural flow.
{=EQzHDnlS}At any rate, I'll fight for any man willing to take the same risks that his men face.
{=VZvFRGVj}I studied the sword to perfect myself. Now everyone wants me to choose a side.
{=B3UQTCRE}Refill my glass and I'll tell you.

{=tes9mQpC}My father traded through Nagasaki, where I first saw Dutch books, foreign instruments, and machines unlike anything made in Japan. While other boys practiced the sword, I struggled through foreign texts, determined to understand the secrets they contained.

{=8D9bBLDI}The more I learned, the clearer it became that the outside world was changing faster than we were. Some say Western knowledge is poison. Others worship it without question. I think both are fools.

{=ZirqXvvL}I do not seek to make Japan into the West. I only wish to learn whatever can strengthen her. So I travel where knowledge can be found, serving any lord wise enough to value skill over tradition alone.
{=0SnKUaex}No doubt a sad state of affairs. So what do you do?
{=WQCAanal}Ah, the old days. And no doubt back then they complained about the older days. I've heard enough.

{=QxLnNYYP}Well, I can't just sit around and drink myself to death, so I sell my sword to anyone worth following. I'm a good trainer - I don't bother with horsemen or archers, but if you've got good steady footmen I can do a lot with them.
{=eTnx78E4}Most men think the world ends at Japan's shores. I know better.
{=1Slubhxc}It's not many who ask that question.

{=STrkPNAu}I spent years riding between castle towns carrying my lord's messages. Most were dullΓÇötax records, supply requests, invitations to banquetsΓÇöbut now and then I was entrusted with letters sealed so tightly that men would kill to read them. I never broke a seal. I never asked questions. A messenger who lives long learns when not to be curious.

{=GwBLUOvp}Still, it was impossible not to notice the country changing. Every road carried more soldiers than merchants. Every castle wanted rifles, powder, or foreign books. Men who smiled at one another in spring refused to speak by autumn.
{=Q24HJPaK}When my lord died, his heir dismissed half the household to save money. I kept my horse and my knowledge of the roads. Those have served me better than any official seal ever did.
{=0SnKUaex}No doubt a sad state of affairs. So what do you do?
{=mR659A6K}What? Does no one respect messengers anymore?
{=udY7HF3U}Well, I can't just sit around and drink myself to death, so I sell my sword to anyone worth following. I'm a good scout, anything you want me to find I will.
{=6Jv713W9}If you carry enough letters, you begin to understand the people who write them.
